candidates.name: rOpenGov/eurostat
candidates.what_it_holds: R package (part of rOpenGov, 1400+ commits, actively maintained, CRAN-published) providing a client for the Eurostat REST/SDMX API: search, download, and cache any Eurostat table by its dataset code, including the collaborative-economy accommodation tables Eurostat produced from the Airbnb/Booking/Expedia/TripAdvisor data-sharing pilot (e.g. tour_ce_omr, tour_ce_omn12 — the same series noted as already held in CONTEXT.md). No data files committed to the repo itself; it is a reproducible pull method, and Eurostat's bulk-download files carry release/vintage timestamps, so this could support a point-in-time re-pull of the platform-nights series rather than a single static CSV.
candidates.why_useful: Turns the Eurostat collaborative-economy series (gap area: point-in-time platform tourism data) into a scriptable, repeatable pull, and could be adapted to fetch the vintage/revision history of tour_ce_omr for gap #4 (point-in-time macro/consensus vintages) instead of a one-off static pull.
candidates.size_hint: package source only, no bundled data
candidates.license: not confirmed from fetched page (CRAN package, commonly GPL/BSD-family for rOpenGov projects)
candidates.last_activity: active as of 2026 (version 4.1.0.9008 referenced on the repo's README)
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: We already hold Eurostat tour_ce_omr 2018-2026; this is a different acquisition path (API client vs. static pull), not the same artifact.

candidates.name: dr-leo/pandaSDMX
candidates.what_it_holds: Python package implementing the SDMX 2.1 standard, with built-in connectors for Eurostat, ECB, OECD, World Bank, ILO, BIS, UNICEF and the UN statistics division. Apache-2.0 licensed, 134 stars, 928 commits, actively developed (readthedocs docs current).
candidates.why_useful: One client can pull Eurostat platform-tourism tables, ECB series (FX, rates, sentiment), and OECD tourism/consumer-confidence tables through a single, scriptable SDMX interface — useful as generic tooling for the OECD/ECB/Eurostat legs of this theme rather than a dataset itself.
candidates.last_activity: active, commits through 2023+ per repo metadata (exact date not confirmed)

candidates.name: expersso/OECD
candidates.what_it_holds: R package (145 stars, 66 commits) wrapping the OECD Data Explorer / SDMX API for programmatic, reproducible retrieval of any OECD dataset via get_dataset()/get_data_structure(); not tourism-specific out of the box but works against OECD's full catalogue including tourism and consumer-confidence series.
candidates.why_useful: Generic, scriptable path to OECD tourism/platform-economy tables (e.g. any OECD Tourism Trends & Policies or Digital Economy Outlook series) beyond whatever static OECD consumer-confidence panel we already hold.
candidates.last_activity: not confirmed (66 commits total, unclear recency)
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: We already hold an OECD consumer confidence panel; this is a generic access method for other OECD tables, not the same data.

notes: This theme returned very little direct signal. Extensive web search (WebSearch budget was already exhausted for this session before any query could run — all WebSearch calls returned 'session has used its web search budget'), so all searching was done via WebFetch against Bing/DuckDuckGo result pages and via gh search repos (used all 4 allowed calls). Bing/DDG result pages fetched through WebFetch are frequently low-signal for this kind of niche technical query: the summarizing pass often only sees generic navigational/homepage links (github.com/login, github.com/signup, etc.) rather than actual ranked results, and several queries returned completely off-topic results (concert tours, cricket boards, racing content) due to keyword collisions with 'ECB', 'tour', etc. lite.duckduckgo.com and html.duckduckgo.com both failed with connection errors. github.com/search (the HTML search endpoint) returned HTTP 429 on essentially every attempt, so most verification had to go through direct repo/org URLs instead of GitHub's own search. gh search repos on GitHub's API (4 calls used, as allowed) found no relevant repositories at all for 'eurostat airbnb', 'collaborative economy platform tourism', 'short-term rental platform data', 'airbnb europe eurostat', 'platform economy statistics', or 'tourism statistics europe' — only one irrelevant hit ('OECD-Tourism-Data-Mining', empty/no description, 0 stars) for 'oecd tourism data'. Checking known official GitHub orgs directly (github.com/eurostat, github.com/ONSdigital, github.com/orgs/ec-jrc) found no tourism/platform-economy/Airbnb repositories among their public repos — Eurostat's org is all mapping/geodata tooling, ONS Digital's is all census/survey infrastructure, and ec-jrc has no tourism-tagged repos. My honest assessment: the actual outputs of the Eurostat-Airbnb/Booking/Expedia/TripAdvisor data-sharing agreement (the tour_ce_* tables) live in Eurostat's own data browser, not as a GitHub-hosted dataset or companion repo, and I could not find any academic-paper replication package (ECB, IMF, OECD) with a public GitHub companion specific to Airbnb/platform tourism either — those working papers, where they exist, do not appear to publish code/data on GitHub (or it's not discoverable through the search paths available in this run). The three candidates I am flagging are all generic SDMX/API-client tooling (rOpenGov/eurostat, pandaSDMX, expersso/OECD) that COULD be pointed at the relevant Eurostat/OECD/ECB tables reproducibly, including possibly at vintage/point-in-time pulls, but none of them are Airbnb-specific datasets or repos, and none fill a numbered gap directly — they're process tooling at best. A more promising path for a future scout on this exact theme would be: (a) searching Zenodo/Dataverse directly (not via GitHub) for the actual Eurostat pilot project deliverables and any national-statistics-office (INSEE, Destatis, CBS Netherlands, INE Spain) 'collaborative economy' methodology reports, since several EU national statistical offices ran their own platform-data studies as part of the same agreement and may have published data appendices there rather than on GitHub; (b) trying GitHub's code-search (not repo-search) for literal strings like 'tour_ce_omr' or 'collaborative economy accommodation' inside notebooks, which repo-search does not reach; (c) checking RePEc/IDEAS for ECB/IMF working papers on platform tourism and following their 'Software/data' links, which sometimes point to GitHub even when the repos themselves don't mention Eurostat/OECD/IMF in their names or descriptions.
